messages:
sam: Heads-up — ran a targeted stress pass on the shared GPU pool in us-west last night. Noticed medium tenants holding long KV sessions and starving higher-SLA requests. Thinking about implementing adaptive priority lanes + "cold-pool" fallback to contain noisy neighbors. Thoughts?
lia: Can you drop the grafana panels/short numbers? :eyes:
sam: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/shared-pool-summary — 95th->99.9th latency divergence during sustained 30m window, concurrent KV sessions per-tenant spiked to 350 for a few tenants, overall GPU util ~92%. Demotion events correlated with 5–10% increase in premium tail.
devon: Cold-pool = CPU-backed nodes where requests are queued and served slower but cheaper? What's the demotion trigger?
sam: Exactly. Goal is graceful degradation: tenants who breach a rolling fair-use threshold get routed to cold-pool (CPU, larger queue, no KV hot sessions) until their burst cools off. Demotion trigger proposal: rolling 1m token/sec > tenant_quota * 1.5 OR sustained KV session time > 12s for 60s window.
yun: Risk note: moving to cold-pool increases client retries which can amplify load. Need admission + backoff at the gateway and a per-tenant circuit damper that reduces concurrency vs just moving to cold nodes.
ops-nora: Metrics we should track from day 1: demotion_rate (per-tenant), demotion_duration_p50/95/99, retry_rate_after_demotion, e2e_premium_99.9, cold_pool_cpu_iowait, cost_delta_per_hour. Also tag demotions by reason (tokens, KV, infra).
sam: Agreed. Proposed simple config (will refine in PR):
```
admission:
  lanes:
    - name: premium
      weight: 4
      max_inflight: 120
    - name: standard
      weight: 2
      max_inflight: 60
    - name: cold
      weight: 1
      max_inflight: 20
  demotion:
    token_threshold_multiplier: 1.5
    kv_latency_sustained: 12s
    demote_window: 60s
    cooldown: 300s
```
lia: Can we make weights dynamic by SLA credits? e.g., premium tenants with unused credits temporarily get extra weight.
devon: Yes — compute effective weight = base_weight * (1 + min(credits/1000, 1.5)). Keep a cap. That also helps smooth churn.
yun: Implementation detail: we should maintain a per-tenant leaky-bucket measured at the edge and a short-lived token allocation for the serving mesh. Avoid central sync on every request.
ops-nora: Rollout plan suggestion: feature-flagged in us-west, 5% tenants canonical canary (include mix of premium+standard), enable synthetic noisy tenants to validate demotion and recovery, wait 48h, expand to 25%, then region-wide. Alerts on demotion_rate > 2% or premium_99.9 regressed > 15% jump.
sam: Who can own the PR and the canary? @devon? :thumbsup:
devon: I can own the PR + canary orchestration. Will sketch the mesh hook and the gateway token bucket.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Created canary feature-flag: adaptive-priority-lanes/us-west (expires in 30d). :white_check_mark:
lia: Add a dashboard row for "demotion reasons" and a panel with top-10 tenants by demotion time. Also add a pager rule for demotion_rate sustained > 5% for 30m.
yun: One more thought — implement a soft grace reclaim: when a tenant is demoted, let them keep 1 hot-KV session for 10s to avoid immediate retry storms. Small window prevents thundering-herd.
ops-nora: Costs: expect cold-pool to be ~6x cheaper per-query but 3–5x slower. We should model cost vs latency SLO loss in a simple spreadsheet before enabling wide. I'll make one and post.
sam: Great. I'll open the RFC PR with config + graphs + rollout checklist, assign to @devon and @lia. Meeting to sync tomorrow 09:30 PT if needed. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
